<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Implement Quality slice">
Implement the Quality slice in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: CleanerCrm.Quality context (ChecklistTemplate, Checklist, ChecklistItem, Photo, IncidentReport schemas + Scorecard module + migrations) and CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive (Review + Scorecards LiveViews) with routes.

FIRST: call mcp start_task with requirement_name="implementation_file", entity_type="component", module_name="CleanerCrm.Quality", then for each child/surface per the prompts (ChecklistTemplate, Checklist, ChecklistItem, Photo, IncidentReport, Scorecard, CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.Review, CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.Scorecards). If module_name isn't accepted, resolve via list_requirements module_filter="Quality".

Acceptance contracts (read ALL before coding): test/spex/839_*/ (owner review + scorecards + photo timestamps + chargeback proof), test/spex/842_*/ (room-grouped checklist, check-off, photo attach, completion blocked with required unchecked, offline upload retry) and test/spex/845_*/ (incident reports: photo required for damage/missing-item, NOT unsafe-condition; immutable; auto timestamp+cleaner; office notified). The FieldLive.Job surface those specs drive does NOT exist yet (another agent builds it later) — your context API must support it: expose functions for checklist instantiation per job, item check-off, photo attach (upload state pending→uploaded per ADR file-storage; local storage adapter behind a behaviour is fine for now, no live S3), completion gating, incident filing, and scorecard aggregation. QualityLive routes ~p"/quality" (Review) and ~p"/quality/scorecards". Also honor the existing fixtures contract: CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture calls CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}...]) — implement that exact function. Scope by account; audit via Audit.Recorder where sensible.

Depends on CleanerCrm.Scheduling (stable, read-only) and Clients (read-only). Do NOT modify scheduling*, schedule_live/*, client_live/*, quoting*, notifications*, billing*, audit_live (other agents own them).

Verify: mix compile clean, mix format, MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate, `mix spex test/spex/839_review_photo_proof_and_quality_scorecards_per_job/` (criteria not needing FieldLive may pass; report counts), `mix test` no regressions.

Final response: files, 839/842/845 pass counts, what stays blocked on FieldLive. Under 150 words.
</teammate-message>

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Generate the implementation for a Phoenix component.

Project: Cleaner CRM
Project Description: 
Component Name: Quality
Component Description: Room-by-room checklists from per-property templates, before/after photo proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions), and per-cleaner quality scorecards
Type: context

Spec File: .code_my_spec/spec/cleaner_crm/quality.spec.md
Test File: test/cleaner_crm/quality_test.exs

Implementation Instructions:
1. Read the spec file to understand the component architecture
2. Read the test file to understand the expected behavior and any test fixtures
3. Create all necessary module files following the component spec
4. Implement all public API functions specified in the spec
5. Ensure the implementation satisfies the tests
6. Create schemas, migrations, or supporting code as needed


Coding Rules:
You are Jose Valim, creator of the Elixir Language.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder do
  @moduledoc """
  API other contexts call to append audit trail entries.

  Callers pass the acting scope, an action string, the subject being
  changed, and old/new value maps. Nothing here ever updates or deletes
  a row — this module only ever inserts.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the scope's current user.
  """
  def record(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    %AuditEntry{}
    |> AuditEntry.changeset(%{
      account_id: account_id,
      actor_id: scope.user && scope.user.id,
      system: false,
      action: action,
      subject_type: subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries for a subject, most recent first.
  """
  def list_for_subject(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, subject_type, subject_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where(
      [e],
      e.account_id == ^account_id and e.subject_type == ^subject_type and
        e.subject_id == ^subject_id
    )
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end
end

=== criterion_7161_cleaner_completes_a_job_with_a_fully_checked_checklist_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story839.Criterion7161Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 839 — Review photo proof and quality scorecards per job
  Criterion 7161 — Cleaner completes a job with a fully checked checklist
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner checks off every checklist task and completes the job" do
    scenario "cleaner completes a job with a fully checked checklist" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{owner_conn: owner_conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with a checklist", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana checks off every task on the checklist, including the optional one", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        Enum.each(context.checklist.items, fn item ->
          job_live
          |> element("[data-test='checklist-item-#{item.id}']")
          |> render_click()
        end)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      when_ "Ana marks the job complete", context do
        context.job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to Ana", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees every task checked off when reviewing the job", context do
        {:ok, _review_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/quality/#{context.job.id}")

        for item <- context.checklist.items do
          assert html =~ item.task
        end

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story839.Criterion7163Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 839 — Review photo proof and quality scorecards per job
  Criterion 7163 — Cleaner tries to complete with unchecked required tasks
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner tries to finish a job while a required task is still unchecked" do
    scenario "cleaner tries to complete with unchecked required tasks" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with two required tasks", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana checks off only one of the two required tasks", context do
        [first_required | _] = Enum.filter(context.checklist.items, & &1.required)

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='checklist-item-#{first_required.id}']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      when_ "Ana tries to mark the job complete", context do
        html =
          context.job_live
          |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
          |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html_after_attempt, html)}
      end

      then_ "the job is not marked complete", context do
        refute render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "Ana is prompted to check off or mark the remaining task skipped with a reason",
            context do
        [_first_required, second_required] = Enum.filter(context.checklist.items, & &1.required)

        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='incomplete-required-tasks-warning']")
        assert context.html_after_attempt =~ second_required.task

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='skip-task-#{second_required.id}-button']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared givens for Cleaner CRM BDD specs.

  Consumer spex modules pull these in with a plain Elixir `import`:

      import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

      scenario "..." do
        given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account
      end

  | Name | Produces | Requires |
  |---|---|---|
  | `:logged_in_owner_with_account` | `context.conn` (authenticated), `context.user`, `context.scope`, `context.account` | `context.conn` |
  """

  use SexySpex.Givens

  import Phoenix.ConnTest
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

  register_given :logged_in_owner_with_account, context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture() |> Fixtures.set_password()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, login_live, _html} = live(context.conn, "/users/log-in")

    form =
      form(login_live, "#login_form_password",
        user: %{
          email: user.email,
          password: Fixtures.valid_user_password(),
          remember_me: true
        }
      )

    conn = submit_form(form, context.conn)

    {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

1	# Photo & File Storage — S3-compatible object storage with presigned uploads
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Stories 842 (before/after checklist photos, offline-tolerant), 845 (incident report photos), and 839 (owner photo review) make photo capture a core flow from phones on cell connections. Payroll CSV exports (838) also need file delivery. Photos must be durable, cheap, and uploaded without proxying large bodies through the app server.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **S3-compatible object storage + presigned URLs** — direct-from-phone uploads via LiveView `allow_upload(external: ...)`; works with AWS S3, Hetzner Object Storage, or Tigris.
12	- **Local disk on the app server** — simplest but not durable across deploys and complicates Hetzner scaling.
13	- **Cloudinary/Uploadcare** — image pipelines we don't need yet at meaningful cost.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Store photos in S3-compatible object storage (Hetzner Object Storage to match the Hetzner deployment ADR; any S3 API works). Generate presigned PUT URLs server-side with a small project-local signer (no ExAws dependency — Req + :crypto SigV4), and use LiveView external uploads so phones upload directly. `CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo` records track upload state (`pending` → `uploaded`) to tolerate offline retry (criterion 7172).
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- Bucket credentials via Dotenvy; per-company key prefixes for tenant isolation.
22	- Thumbnails/derivatives deferred; store originals, render responsive via `img` sizing initially.
23	- A cleanup job (Oban) reaps `pending` photo records whose uploads never completed.
24

# Photo & File Storage — S3-compatible object storage with presigned uploads

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Stories 842 (before/after checklist photos, offline-tolerant), 845 (incident report photos), and 839 (owner photo review) make photo capture a core flow from phones on cell connections. Payroll CSV exports (838) also need file delivery. Photos must be durable, cheap, and uploaded without proxying large bodies through the app server.

## Options Considered

- **S3-compatible object storage + presigned URLs** — direct-from-phone uploads via LiveView `allow_upload(external: ...)`; works with AWS S3, Hetzner Object Storage, or Tigris.
- **Local disk on the app server** — simplest but not durable across deploys and complicates Hetzner scaling.
- **Cloudinary/Uploadcare** — image pipelines we don't need yet at meaningful cost.

## Decision

Store photos in S3-compatible object storage (Hetzner Object Storage to match the Hetzner deployment ADR; any S3 API works). Generate presigned PUT URLs server-side with a small project-local signer (no ExAws dependency — Req + :crypto SigV4), and use LiveView external uploads so phones upload directly. `CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo` records track upload state (`pending` → `uploaded`) to tolerate offline retry (criterion 7172).

## Consequences

- Bucket credentials via Dotenvy; per-company key prefixes for tenant isolation.
- Thumbnails/derivatives deferred; store originals, render responsive via `img` sizing initially.
- A cleanup job (Oban) reaps `pending` photo records whose uploads never completed.

1	# Cleaner Field Experience — mobile-responsive LiveView, SMS as the loud channel
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Stories 841–845 are the cleaner's daily surface, used on phones, sometimes with poor connectivity. Research: cleaners are non-technical, onboarding budget is near zero (200–400% turnover in janitorial), and silent schedule changes are the top cause of missed cleanings. Incumbent gap: tech-only native apps with no office counterpart, or no cleaner app at all.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **Mobile-responsive LiveView (PWA-lite)** — one codebase, no app-store friction ("learnable in one shift", installable via home-screen), consistent with the stack.
12	- **Native app (Swift/Kotlin or React Native)** — better offline and push, but doubles the codebase and adds store review latency; kills MVP velocity.
13	- **LiveView Native** — promising but too immature to bet the core persona surface on.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Build the cleaner surface as mobile-first responsive LiveView under `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive`, with large touch targets and minimal navigation. The "loud, acknowledged" alert channel (843) is SMS (already required for client reminders) deep-linking into the field app, where acknowledgment is recorded; unacknowledged alerts escalate to the office. Web Push can be added later without changing the model. Offline tolerance is scoped to photo-upload retry (LiveView external uploads with pending state), not full offline operation.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- No app-store presence at MVP; marketing implication accepted.
22	- True offline mode (viewing jobs with no signal) is deferred; job briefs render fast and cacheable, but live features need connectivity.
23	- SMS cost per alert is accepted as the price of reliability; per-message delivery status already tracked by the SMS ADR.
24

# Cleaner Field Experience — mobile-responsive LiveView, SMS as the loud channel

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Stories 841–845 are the cleaner's daily surface, used on phones, sometimes with poor connectivity. Research: cleaners are non-technical, onboarding budget is near zero (200–400% turnover in janitorial), and silent schedule changes are the top cause of missed cleanings. Incumbent gap: tech-only native apps with no office counterpart, or no cleaner app at all.

## Options Considered

- **Mobile-responsive LiveView (PWA-lite)** — one codebase, no app-store friction ("learnable in one shift", installable via home-screen), consistent with the stack.
- **Native app (Swift/Kotlin or React Native)** — better offline and push, but doubles the codebase and adds store review latency; kills MVP velocity.
- **LiveView Native** — promising but too immature to bet the core persona surface on.

## Decision

Build the cleaner surface as mobile-first responsive LiveView under `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive`, with large touch targets and minimal navigation. The "loud, acknowledged" alert channel (843) is SMS (already required for client reminders) deep-linking into the field app, where acknowledgment is recorded; unacknowledged alerts escalate to the office. Web Push can be added later without changing the model. Offline tolerance is scoped to photo-upload retry (LiveView external uploads with pending state), not full offline operation.

## Consequences

- No app-store presence at MVP; marketing implication accepted.
- True offline mode (viewing jobs with no signal) is deferred; job briefs render fast and cacheable, but live features need connectivity.
- SMS cost per alert is accepted as the price of reliability; per-message delivery status already tracked by the SMS ADR.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.CreateAuditEntriesTable do
  use Ecto.Migration

  def change do
    create table(:audit_entries, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :actor_id, references(:users, on_delete: :nilify_all)
      add :system, :boolean, null: false, default: false
      add :action, :string, null: false
      add :subject_type, :string, null: false
      add :subject_id, :binary_id, null: false
      add :old_value, :map, null: false, default: %{}
      add :new_value, :map, null: false, default: %{}

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
    end

    create index(:audit_entries, [:account_id])
    create index(:audit_entries, [:subject_type, :subject_id])

    # Defense in depth: audit entries are append-only. Application code
    # never exposes update/delete; these rules block it even if it did.
    execute(
      "CREATE RULE audit_entries_no_update AS ON UPDATE TO audit_entries DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS audit_entries_no_update ON audit_entries"
    )

    execute(
      "CREATE RULE audit_entries_no_delete AS ON DELETE TO audit_entries DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS audit_entries_no_delete ON audit_entries"
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Property do
  @moduledoc """
  A serviced location with address, parking, pet, and access-detail
  notes (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, emergency contact).

  Every property belongs to exactly one client. Lockbox and alarm
  codes are stored encrypted at rest — see `CleanerCrm.Encrypted.Binary`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Encrypted

  @access_detail_fields ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code parking_notes pet_notes
                            emergency_contact_name emergency_contact_phone)a

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          service_address: String.t() | nil,
          entry_method: String.t() | nil,
          lockbox_code: String.t() | nil,
          alarm_code: String.t() | nil,
          parking_notes: String.t() | nil,
          pet_notes: String.t() | nil,
          emergency_contact_name: String.t() | nil,
          emergency_contact_phone: String.t() | nil,
          client: CleanerCrm.Clients.Client.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "properties" do
    field :service_address, :string
    field :entry_method, :string
    field :lockbox_code, Encrypted.Binary
    field :alarm_code, Encrypted.Binary
    field :parking_notes, :string
    field :pet_notes, :string
    field :emergency_contact_name, :string
    field :emergency_contact_phone, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @doc """
  Fields whose changes are sensitive enough to warrant an audit entry
  when updated (see `CleanerCrm.Clients.update_property/3`).
  """
  def access_code_fields, do: ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code)a

  def changeset(property, attrs) do
    property
    |> cast(blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), [:client_id, :service_address | @access_detail_fields])
    |> validate_required([:client_id, :service_address], message: "is required")
    |> assoc_constraint(:client)
  end

  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(%{"client_id" => ""} = attrs), do: %{attrs | "client_id" => nil}
  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), do: attrs
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
---scope---
defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

22	  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.

24	  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page
  # would otherwise see a permanently nil `active_account_id`. Until
  # that selection is persisted, default a signed-in user onto one of
  # their accounts — the common case is a single-account owner, for
  # whom this is unambiguous.
  defp scope_with_active_account(nil), do: Scope.for_user(nil)

  defp scope_with_active_account(user) do
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(%{method: "GET"} = conn) do
    put_session(conn, :user_return_to, current_path(conn))
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(conn), do: conn
end

  @moduledoc """
  A reusable room-by-room task template for a property or service
  type, from which a job's own `CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist` can be
  instantiated (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.instantiate_checklist/3`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  defmodule TemplateItem do
    @moduledoc """
    One room/task line on a template, embedded — a template is a
    small, template-owned list, not something referenced elsewhere,
    so it lives inline rather than as its own table.
    """

    use Ecto.Schema
    import Ecto.Changeset

    @type t :: %__MODULE__{
            room: String.t() | nil,
            task: String.t() | nil,
            required: boolean()
          }

    @primary_key false
    embedded_schema do
      field :room, :string
      field :task, :string
      field :required, :boolean, default: true
    end

    def changeset(item, attrs) do
      item
      |> cast(attrs, [:room, :task, :required])
      |> validate_required([:task])
    end
  end

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          items: [TemplateItem.t()],
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklist_templates" do
    field :name, :string
    embeds_many :items, TemplateItem, on_replace: :delete

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(template, attrs) do
    template
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :property_id])
    |> cast_embed(:items, with: &TemplateItem.changeset/2)
    |> validate_required([:name])
  end

  @doc """
  This template's items as the flat `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist/4` expects.
  """
  def item_attrs(%__MODULE__{items: items}) do
    Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:room, :task, :required]))
  end
end
