defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem do
  @moduledoc """
  A single room/task line on a job's checklist: its required flag,
  checked/skipped completion state, and the before/after photos
  attached to it as proof.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          room: String.t() | nil,
          task: String.t() | nil,
          required: boolean(),
          checked: boolean(),
          checked_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          skipped: boolean(),
          skip_reason: String.t() | nil,
          position: integer(),
          photos: [Photo.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklist_items" do
    field :room, :string
    field :task, :string
    field :required, :boolean, default: true
    field :checked, :boolean, default: false
    field :checked_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :skipped, :boolean, default: false
    field :skip_reason, :string
    field :position, :integer, default: 0

    belongs_to :checklist, CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist, type: :binary_id
    has_many :photos, Photo

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(item, attrs) do
    item
    |> cast(attrs, [:checklist_id, :room, :task, :required, :position])
    |> validate_required([:checklist_id, :task])
  end

  @doc "Checks the item off, stamping when, and clears any prior skip."
  def check_changeset(item) do
    change(item, checked: true, checked_at: DateTime.utc_now(), skipped: false, skip_reason: nil)
  end

  @doc "Reverts a checked item back to unchecked."
  def uncheck_changeset(item) do
    change(item, checked: false, checked_at: nil)
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped, with a reason, instead of done."
  def skip_changeset(item, reason) do
    item
    |> change(skipped: true, skip_reason: reason, checked: false, checked_at: nil)
    |> validate_required([:skip_reason])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.IncidentReport do
  @moduledoc """
  An immutable, timestamped report of damage, a missing item, or an
  unsafe condition, filed by the cleaner working the job. A photo is
  required for `:damage` and `:missing_item` — something the office
  needs to see to act on — but not `:unsafe_condition`, so a cleaner
  never has to stop and photograph a hazard before reporting it.

  Nothing here, or anywhere else in this context, updates or deletes
  a report once filed — see the migration's DB rules for the
  backstop, mirroring `CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.Photo

  @type type :: :damage | :missing_item | :unsafe_condition

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          type: type() | nil,
          description: String.t() | nil,
          filed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          photos: [Photo.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @photo_required_types [:damage, :missing_item]

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "incident_reports" do
    field :type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:damage, :missing_item, :unsafe_condition]
    field :description, :string
    field :filed_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    has_many :photos, Photo

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
  end

  @doc """
  `has_photo?` reflects whether a photo accompanies this filing (the
  caller inserts it in the same transaction), since a report needing
  one is judged before any `Photo` row necessarily exists.
  """
  def changeset(report, attrs, has_photo?) do
    report
    |> cast(attrs, [:account_id, :job_id, :cleaner_id, :type, :description, :filed_at])
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :job_id, :cleaner_id, :type, :description, :filed_at])
    |> validate_photo_required(has_photo?)
  end

    case get_field(changeset, :type) do
      type when type in @photo_required_types ->
        add_error(changeset, :photo, "is required for this report type")

      _type ->
        changeset
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure scoring math: a single job's quality score, and the
  average/trend across a cleaner's completed jobs. No querying and
  no persistence — `CleanerCrm.Quality` owns fetching the checklists
  and scores this operates on.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist

  @scale 5

  @doc """
  A single checklist's quality score, on a 1-5 scale: the completion
  ratio of its items (checked or skipped-with-reason, over the
  total) scaled to 5, alone until the owner rates the job, then
  blended evenly with that 1-5 rating.

  Expects `checklist.items` preloaded, as returned by
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.get_checklist_for_job/2`.
  """
  def score(%Checklist{items: items, owner_rating: nil}) do
    completion_ratio(items) * @scale
  end

  def score(%Checklist{items: items, owner_rating: rating}) do
    (completion_ratio(items) * @scale + rating) / 2
  end

  defp completion_ratio([]), do: 0.0

  defp completion_ratio(items) do
    done = Enum.count(items, &(&1.checked or &1.skipped))
    done / length(items)
  end

  @doc """
  Aggregates a cleaner's quality scores, given oldest first, into an
  average and a trend (`:up`, `:down`, or `:flat` — comparing the
  average of the first half of jobs against the second).
  """
  def aggregate([]), do: %{average: nil, trend: :flat, count: 0}

  def aggregate(scores) do
    %{average: average(scores), trend: trend(scores), count: length(scores)}
  end

  defp average(scores), do: Enum.sum(scores) / length(scores)

  defp trend(scores) when length(scores) < 2, do: :flat

  defp trend(scores) do
    {first_half, second_half} = Enum.split(scores, div(length(scores), 2))
    compare(average(first_half), average(second_half))
  end

  defp compare(first, second) when second > first, do: :up
  defp compare(first, second) when second < first, do: :down
  defp compare(_first, _second), do: :flat
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} -> insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)

    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_completed",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "completed"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
  checklist's combined quality score.
  """
  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}

    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(scope, job, Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{before_photo: before_photo, after_photo: after_photo}) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [checked.photos, before_photo, after_photo] |> List.flatten() |> Enum.filter(&match?(%Photo{}, &1))}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} -> insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)

    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_completed",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "completed"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
  checklist's combined quality score.
  """
  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}

    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(scope, job, Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{before_photo: before_photo, after_photo: after_photo}) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [checked.photos, before_photo, after_photo] |> List.flatten() |> Enum.filter(&match?(%Photo{}, &1))}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def complete_photo_upload(%Scope{}, %Photo{} = photo, storage_key) do
    photo |> Photo.uploaded_changeset(storage_key) |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Incident reports

  @doc """
  Files an incident report for a job. `attrs` needs `:type`
  (`"damage"`, `"missing_item"`, or `"unsafe_condition"`) and
  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
  """
  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, report} <-
             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
                 "job_id" => job.id,
                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
               }),
               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
             )
             |> Repo.insert() do
          photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
          {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(
      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
        "kind" => "incident",
        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
  """
  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Scorecards

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)
    |> where(
      [c, j],
      c.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        not is_nil(c.completed_at)
    )
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} -> insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a job's checklist with its items and their photos
  preloaded, or `nil` if the job has none yet.
  """
  def get_checklist_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id and c.job_id == ^job_id)
    |> preload(items: :photos)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  @doc """
  Groups a checklist's items by room, in the order each room first
  appears. Items with no room (a flat, unrouted checklist) are
  grouped under `nil`.
  """
  def group_by_room(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    rooms = Enum.uniq_by(items, & &1.room) |> Enum.map(& &1.room)
    grouped = Enum.group_by(items, & &1.room)
    Enum.map(rooms, &{&1, Map.fetch!(grouped, &1)})
  end

  @doc "`{checked_count, total_count}` across a checklist's items."
  def progress(%Checklist{items: items}), do: {Enum.count(items, & &1.checked), length(items)}

  @doc """
  Toggles a checklist item's checked state. Checking an item clears
  any prior skip.
  """
  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{checked: true} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.uncheck_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  def toggle_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc "Marks a required item skipped instead of done, with a reason."
  def skip_checklist_item(%Scope{}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, reason) do
    item |> ChecklistItem.skip_changeset(reason) |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  The required items still blocking completion: unchecked and not
  skipped. Empty means the checklist is ready to complete.
  """
  def incomplete_required_items(%Checklist{items: items}) do
    Enum.filter(items, &(&1.required and not &1.checked and not &1.skipped))
  end

  @doc """
  Completes a job's checklist: refused with the still-incomplete
  required items when any remain; otherwise the checklist is stamped
  done, scored, and the job itself is marked completed.
  """
  def complete_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Checklist{} = checklist) do
    case incomplete_required_items(checklist) do
      [] -> do_complete_job(scope, checklist)
      incomplete -> {:error, {:incomplete_required_tasks, incomplete}}
    end
  end

  defp do_complete_job(scope, checklist) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, completed} <- mark_checklist_completed(checklist),
           {:ok, _job} <- mark_job_completed(scope, completed.job_id) do
        {:ok, completed}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp mark_checklist_completed(checklist) do
    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{
      completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
    })
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp mark_job_completed(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, job_id) do
    job = Job |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id) |> Repo.get!(job_id)

    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :completed}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_completed",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "completed"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Records the owner's 1-5 quality rating for a job, recomputing the
  checklist's combined quality score.
  """
  def rate_job(%Scope{}, %Checklist{} = checklist, rating) do
    rated = %{checklist | owner_rating: rating}

    checklist
    |> Checklist.changeset(%{owner_rating: rating, quality_score: Scorecard.score(rated)})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist already fully checked off with
  before/after photo proof, for callers that seed a completed job's
  proof of work directly (see
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture/3`) rather
  than driving the checklist item by item. `items` is a list of
  `%{task:, before_photo:, after_photo:}` maps.
  """
  def complete_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, items)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             create_checklist(scope, job, Enum.map(items, &Map.take(&1, [:task, :room, :required]))) do
        checked_items =
          checklist.items
          |> Enum.zip(items)
          |> Enum.map(fn {item, proof} -> check_with_photos!(account_id, item, proof) end)

        checklist = %{checklist | items: checked_items}

        checklist
        |> Checklist.changeset(%{
          completed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          quality_score: Scorecard.score(checklist)
        })
        |> Repo.update()
      end
    end)
  end

  defp check_with_photos!(account_id, item, %{before_photo: before_photo, after_photo: after_photo}) do
    checked = item |> ChecklistItem.check_changeset() |> Repo.update!()
    before = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :before, before_photo)
    aftr = insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, checked, :after, after_photo)
    %{checked | photos: [before, aftr]}
  end

  defp insert_checklist_photo!(account_id, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, storage_key) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(%{
      checklist_item_id: item.id,
      kind: kind,
      upload_state: :uploaded,
      storage_key: storage_key,
      captured_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc "Attaches a before/after photo to a checklist item, `:pending` until uploaded."
  def attach_photo(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %ChecklistItem{} = item, kind, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and kind in [:before, :after] do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(Map.merge(%{checklist_item_id: item.id, kind: kind}, attrs))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Flips a pending photo to uploaded once its bytes land in storage."
  def complete_photo_upload(%Scope{}, %Photo{} = photo, storage_key) do
    photo |> Photo.uploaded_changeset(storage_key) |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Incident reports

  @doc """
  Files an incident report for a job. `attrs` needs `:type`
  (`"damage"`, `"missing_item"`, or `"unsafe_condition"`) and
  `:description`; a `:photo` (the same attrs `attach_photo/4` takes)
  is required unless `:type` is `"unsafe_condition"`. The cleaner and
  filing time are always the caller's and now — never accepted from
  `attrs` — and nothing about a filed report can change afterward.
  """
  def file_incident_report(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id, user: user}, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    {photo_attrs, report_attrs} = attrs |> stringify_keys() |> Map.pop("photo")

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, report} <-
             %IncidentReport{account_id: account_id}
             |> IncidentReport.changeset(
               Map.merge(report_attrs, %{
                 "job_id" => job.id,
                 "cleaner_id" => user && user.id,
                 "filed_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
               }),
               not is_nil(photo_attrs)
             )
             |> Repo.insert() do
          photo = photo_attrs && insert_incident_photo!(account_id, report, photo_attrs)
          {:ok, %{report | photos: Enum.filter([photo], & &1)}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp stringify_keys(attrs), do: Map.new(attrs, fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)

  defp insert_incident_photo!(account_id, %IncidentReport{} = report, photo_attrs) do
    %Photo{account_id: account_id}
    |> Photo.changeset(
      Map.merge(stringify_keys(photo_attrs), %{
        "incident_report_id" => report.id,
        "kind" => "incident",
        "upload_state" => "uploaded",
        "captured_at" => DateTime.utc_now()
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists an account's incident reports, most recently filed first,
  with job (and its client), cleaner, and photos preloaded.
  """
  def list_incident_reports(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    IncidentReport
    |> where([r], r.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([r], desc: r.filed_at)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :photos, job: [:client, :property]])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Scorecards

  @doc """
  The cleaner's average quality score and trend across their
  completed jobs, oldest first (see `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`).
  """
  def cleaner_scorecard(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Checklist
    |> join(:inner, [c], j in Job, on: j.id == c.job_id)
    |> where(
      [c, j],
      c.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        not is_nil(c.completed_at)
    )
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.completed_at)
    |> select([c], c.quality_score)
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
    |> Scorecard.aggregate()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality.Checklist do
  @moduledoc """
  The instantiated checklist for a single job: its items, the
  owner's optional 1-5 rating, and the computed quality score (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.Scorecard`). Functions that need `items` for
  scoring or completion gating expect them preloaded, as returned by
  `CleanerCrm.Quality.get_checklist_for_job/2`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistItem

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          checklist_template_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          owner_rating: integer() | nil,
          quality_score: float() | nil,
          completed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          items: [ChecklistItem.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "checklists" do
    field :owner_rating, :integer
    field :quality_score, :float
    field :completed_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :checklist_template, CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate, type: :binary_id

    has_many :items, ChecklistItem, preload_order: [asc: :position]

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(checklist, attrs) do
    checklist
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :job_id,
      :checklist_template_id,
      :owner_rating,
      :quality_score,
      :completed_at
    ])
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> validate_number(:owner_rating, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, less_than_or_equal_to: 5)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })
      )

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                    Can be specified multiple times
    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

## Examples

I've implemented the Quality slice and reported the results to the team lead. Summary:

**Built:** `CleanerCrm.Quality` context (`lib/cleaner_crm/quality.ex`) with schemas `ChecklistTemplate`, `Checklist`, `ChecklistItem`, `Photo`, `IncidentReport`, and a pure `Scorecard` aggregation module, plus `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.Review` (`/quality`, `/quality/:job_id`) and `QualityLive.Scorecards` (`/quality/scorecards`), backed by a new migration creating the five tables (with append-only DB rules on `incident_reports`, mirroring `audit_entries`).

**Bug caught in shared fixtures:** another agent had introduced a `scoped_to_account/1` workaround because spex `given_` blocks bind `scope` before `account_fixture` sets `active_account_id`. Three of my fixture-facing functions (`job_with_proof_of_work_fixture`, `job_with_checklist_fixture`, `job_with_room_checklist_fixture`) were still passing the raw, unscoped `scope` into `Quality.*` calls, which guard on a non-nil account id — this would have crashed every test using them. Fixed by applying the same wrapper.

**Verification:** `mix compile` and `mix format` clean, migration applied, `mix test` shows 140 tests/0 failures (no regressions). Spex: 839 passes 3 of 7 criteria (score computation, cleaner scorecard trend, chargeback photo proof — none touch the field app); the other 4 in 839, all 7 in 842, and all 6 in 845 fail solely on `no route found for GET /field/jobs/:id`, since `FieldLive.Job` hasn't been built yet by its owning agent — not a Quality defect.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })
      )

    job

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

content.text:
I have all the information needed. Here is the full report.

---

**1. `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex`** — exists (229 lines), read in full.

Yes, it lazily creates a checklist. In `defp load_checklist(socket)` at lines 186-201:

```elixir
defp load_checklist(socket) do
  scope = socket.assigns.current_scope
  job = socket.assigns.job

  checklist =
    case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [])
        checklist

      checklist ->
        checklist
    end

  assign(socket, :checklist, checklist)
end
```

The comment directly above it (lines 180-185) explains the intent: "Every job gets a checklist to complete through, even a trivially empty one for a job nothing ever assigned a template to — lazily instantiated here so `ChecklistComponent`'s completion flow ... is the one path every job completes through."

Note it currently calls `Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [])` (an empty item list), not `Quality.instantiate_checklist/3` with a template — there is no template lookup/selection happening here at all today.

`load_checklist/1` is called from `mount/3` (line 116, via the pipeline at lines 111-118) after `job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, id)` (line 108). `socket.assigns.job` is fully available at that point. `Scheduling.get_job!/2` (see scheduling.ex line 28-33) preloads `[:cleaner, :property, :client]`, so `job.property` is preloaded (a `%CleanerCrm.Clients.Property{}` struct, not `Ecto.Association.NotLoaded`), and `job.property_id` is a plain field on the Job schema — both are available. `job.client` is also preloaded.

**2. `lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex`** — read in full (393 lines).

No hook/callback/PubSub/Oban mechanism exists for "job created → notify other contexts." `create_job/3` (lines 45-54) only does:
```elixir
def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
    when not is_nil(account_id) do
  with {:ok, job} <-
         %Job{account_id: account_id}
         |> Job.changeset(attrs)
         |> Repo.insert() do
    record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
    {:ok, job}
  end
end
```
`record_job_created/3` (lines 56-62) only writes to the audit trail via `CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder`. No `Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast`, no behaviour/callback list, no Oban job insertion anywhere in the file. `grep` for pubsub/broadcast/behaviour/callback/Oban in this file returns nothing. Whatever triggers checklist instantiation must be driven from the FieldLive/QualityLive side (or Quality itself), not from a hook Scheduling already exposes.

**3. `lib/cleaner_crm/clients/property.ex`** — read in full (73 lines).

Fields: `service_address`, `entry_method`, `lockbox_code` (encrypted), `alarm_code` (encrypted), `parking_notes`, `pet_notes`, `client_preferences`, `emergency_contact_name`, `emergency_contact_phone`, plus `belongs_to :account`, `belongs_to :client`, and timestamps. No association to checklist templates on the `Property` side — the association exists only from the other direction: `ChecklistTemplate` has `belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property` (checklist_template.ex line 57), but `Property` has no `has_many :checklist_templates` or similar back-reference. If you need `property.checklist_templates`, it isn't there yet — you'd query `Quality.list_checklist_templates/1` and filter by `property_id`, or add the inverse association (which would touch `property.ex`, outside your stated boundary).

**4. `lib/cleaner_crm_web/router.ex`** — read in full (175 lines).

Full route list under `live_session :require_authenticated_user` (lines 72-126):
- `/users/settings`, `/users/settings/confirm-email/:token` → UserLive.Settings
- `/accounts`, `/accounts/new`, `/accounts/:id/edit`, `/accounts/picker`, `/accounts/:id`, `/accounts/:id/manage`, `/accounts/:id/members`, `/accounts/:id/invitations`
- `/integrations` → IntegrationLive.Index
- `/clients`, `/clients/new`, `/clients/:id/edit`, `/clients/:id/properties/new`, `/clients/:id`, `/properties/new`, `/properties/:id/edit`, `/properties/:id`
- `/schedule`, `/schedule/plans/new`, `/schedule/plans/:id/edit`, `/schedule/jobs/new`, `/schedule/jobs/:id/assign`, `/schedule/jobs/:id`, `/schedule/cleaners/new`, `/schedule/cleaners/:id`, `/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new`
- `/audit`
- `/quotes`, `/quotes/new`, `/quotes/:id`
- `/quality` → `QualityLive.Review, :index` (line 113)
- `/quality/scorecards` → `QualityLive.Scorecards, :index` (line 114)
- `/quality/:job_id` → `QualityLive.Review, :show` (line 115)
- `/timesheets`
- `/invoices`, `/invoices/:id`
- `/reminders`

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.FormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create/edit a client's name and billing preference. On successful save, navigates to the client's own page directly (rather than notifying the parent to do it) — a parent's `handle_info` reacting to a component's self-sent message runs one mailbox message after the "save" event's own reply, too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to observe the redirect. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|---------------|----------|----------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | client | `Client.t()` | yes | `%Client{}` (blank for `:new`, loaded for `:edit`) | ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Clients @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>{form_title(@action)} <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="client-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:name]} type="text" label="Name" /> <.input field={@form[:card_on_file]} type="checkbox" label="Card on file" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Client
""" end @impl true def update(%{client: client} = assigns, socket) do changeset = Clients.change_client(assigns.current_scope, client) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"client" => client_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Clients.change_client(socket.assigns.client, client_params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end def handle_event("save", %{"client" => client_params}, socket) do save_client(socket, socket.assigns.action, client_params) end defp save_client(socket, :new, params) do case Clients.create_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, client} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/clients/#{client}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp save_client(socket, :edit, params) do case Clients.update_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.client, params) do {:ok, client} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/clients/#{client}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp form_title(:new), do: "New Client" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Client" end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quality do
  @moduledoc """
  Room-by-room checklists instantiated per job, before/after photo
  proof, incident reports (damage, missing items, unsafe conditions),
  and the scorecards that aggregate a cleaner's completed jobs.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Quality.{
    Checklist,
    ChecklistItem,
    ChecklistTemplate,
    IncidentReport,
    Photo,
    Scorecard
  }

  ## Checklist templates

  def list_checklist_templates(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_checklist_template!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_checklist_template(%Scope{}, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template, attrs \\ %{}) do
    ChecklistTemplate.changeset(template, attrs)
  end

  def create_checklist_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %ChecklistTemplate{account_id: account_id}
    |> ChecklistTemplate.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Checklists

  @doc """
  Instantiates a job's checklist from a template, copying its
  room/task/required lines down as the job's own checklist items.
  """
  def instantiate_checklist(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job, %ChecklistTemplate{} = template) do
    create_checklist(scope, job, ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), template_id: template.id)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job's checklist from `items` — each a `%{task:, required:}`
  map, optionally carrying `room:` — in the order given. Every
  checklist item starts unchecked and un-skipped.
  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{id: job_id}, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position) do
    params =
      attrs
      |> Map.new(fn {key, value} -> {to_string(key), value} end)
      |> Map.put("checklist_id", checklist.id)
      |> Map.put_new("position", position)

    %ChecklistItem{}
    |> ChecklistItem.changeset(params)
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  @doc """
